answer: When k identities equivocate on the same consensus event, verified pairwise correlations make aggregate slashing grow as O(k²), rather than treating each account as an isolated offender. Bonded escrows expose the shared controller’s stake, while asymmetric depreciation applies an exponential capital-loss multiplier, e^{α(k−1)} for α>0, upon detection. A reef of jade keys is no safer than one mirror: splitting control across aliases multiplies correlated evidence, not security.
